project-zomboid.note: Production egg #3 (Tekkura UUID). The three PZ plans point at it. Egg #1, renamed "Project Zomboid (old)", stays for the customer server already on it.

ark-survival-ascended.note: Peer port is always game +1, hence 2. RCON is used inside the container for clean shutdown. Its subcategory exists under "Ark: Survival" (hidden until it has products).

ark-survival-evolved.note: Raw UDP is always game +1, query is the 3rd port. The egg default admin password was PleaseChangeMe. Its subcategory exists under "Ark: Survival" (hidden until it has products).

minecraft-paper.note: USER_AGENT defaults to Tekkura's; PaperMC's API refuses downloads without one.

minecraft-vanilla.note: The standard start: Minecraft products point at this egg, and the customer picks their type on the Server type page afterwards.

minecraft-curseforge.note: Needs Tekkura's CurseForge API key as the egg default for API_KEY. Hidden from customers until it is set.

minecraft-modrinth.note: Used by the modpack installer, not shown as a software choice.

palworld.note: RCON stays inside the container (the console uses it), so it needs no allocation.

cs2.note: Steam token made optional: it is the customer's own credential. Without one the server is LAN only.

necesse.note: The port reaches the game through cfg/server.cfg.

unturned.note: Game +1 is required. Steam token made optional and passed only when set.

conan-exiles.note: Game +1 is fixed, query is the 3rd port. Players connect on the game port (1st).

valheim.note: Query is always game +1. The join password defaulted to "secret" on every server; now generated.

valheim-bepinex.note: Query is always game +1. The join password defaulted to "secret" on every server; now generated.

terraria.note: The port reaches the game through serverconfig.txt.

arma-reforger.note: The port reaches the game through config.json. A2S and RCON are optional and off.

windrose.note: Invite codes work without it; DirectIP must match the game port, so it follows port 1.

arma-3.note: Game, +1 query, +2 Steam, +3 VON and +4 BattlEye are fixed offsets, hence a run of 5; RCON (required, no default upstream) gets the 6th. The customer supplies the Steam login (STEAM_USER/STEAM_PASS viewable, editable, optional; on the panel since 2026-10-19). The server builds, the first install stops with the installer's own message until they enter it; once both are filled the panel reinstalls it by itself (eggs.reinstall_variables). Their own account is the only way Workshop mods download, since that needs Arma 3 ownership.

minecraft-quilt.note: Upstream shipped no features; given eula, java_version and pid_limit like the other Java eggs.

minecraft-spongeforge.note: Superseded: the Sponge egg (minecraft-spongevanilla) installs SpongeVanilla, SpongeForge and SpongeNeo through SPONGE_TYPE, and supports current Java. This one stops at Java 18.

minecraft-purpur-geyser.note: Geyser's Bedrock listener is pointed at the server's own port (UDP side) through plugins/Geyser-Spigot/config.yml; Bedrock players use the same address.

minecraft-velocity.note: USER_AGENT defaults to Tekkura's; PaperMC's API refuses downloads without one.

rust.note: Query, web RCON (admin tools) and the Rust+ companion app all need to be reachable, so each gets a port; one spare. RCON password generated.

dayz.note: Query is needed for the server list. Like Arma 3, it installs only with a real Steam login, which the customer supplies; the server reinstalls itself once both are filled.

bot-nodejs.note: Node.js 24 LTS by default, 26 and 22 offered; 23 and 25 dropped (end of life). Running is the entrypoint's `:/home/container$ ` line. Kind bot: no ports by default (required_ports 0 needs the panel's bot kind first, see the panel's docs/PLATFORM-PLAN.md), the web port add-on brings one. With no repository the install leaves a placeholder that prints what to do and idles, so a store order starts and reads Running. Setting GIT_ADDRESS reinstalls by itself (reinstall) and the placeholder is removed first. Checked in Docker on the real images 2026-10-26: no repo, then repo set and reinstalled. Deploy results (2026-10-30): after a checkout or a deploy's pull the egg writes `.tekkura-deploy-result` (`ok|failed <time> <sha>`), which the panel's RecordDeployResultJob reads, since Wings reports an install that exits 1 as successful. Checked on the local stack: a pull recorded ok, and failed with the git server down. On production as egg #41 (2026-10-31), set from this entry.

bot-muse.note: Muse v2.11.8 (MIT), pinned in VERSION, which customers cannot change. Upstream bugs fixed: .env read BOT_TOKEN, which does not exist, so the token was always empty; the Spotify secret was written to the client id line; `yarn install --prod` left out prisma, which Muse runs at every start. Token and YouTube key are optional in the egg (core refuses to build a server with a required variable empty) and listed in the panel's setup_variables, which the bot's overview asks for; until the token is set the startup waits instead of crash looping. Kind bot, ready-made: the egg decides what runs. The program folder is on the file deny list ('*' except data/), so Files and SFTP cannot open or change it; Wings still lists the names. No secret is ever in the startup line: the yolk entrypoint prints that line to the console after Wings fills in ${VARIABLES}, so the token reaches the bot through .env (Wings config file) instead. Checked on the local Docker stack 2026-10-26: bought through the store, built by billing, installed and started on Wings rc.1. The waiting line is a second done string beside Ready!, so a bot waiting for its token reads Running like Game Server Watcher rather than Starting for ever (2026-10-30). On production as egg #43 (2026-10-31), set from this entry.

bot-game-server-watcher.note: a-sync/game-server-watcher v3.1.25 (AGPL-3.0, hosted unmodified), pinned in VERSION. Checked on the local Docker stack 2026-10-26: bought through the store, built by billing, installed and started on Wings rc.1. On production as egg #44 (2026-10-31), set from this entry.

bot-red.note: Red-DiscordBot 3.5.24 (GPL-3.0, hosted unmodified), pinned in VERSION, which customers cannot change; Python 3.11 (Red 3.5 supports up to 3.11). Upstream passed the token as --token {{TOKEN}} in the startup line, which the console prints; Red reads RED_TOKEN from the environment, so the startup sets it from printenv. Upstream's token defaulted to GET_YOUR_OWN and its Owner variable was required with no default and never used (Red takes the application owner); both fixed, Owner dropped. Installed with pip into the server's ~/.local at the pinned version (upstream took whatever was newest) and the instance config is written by the install (upstream fetched it from parkervcp/eggs, an old repository). Data, cogs included, live in data/; everything else is on the file deny list. TMPDIR is the server's .tmp, since pip and the Audio cog fill the container's small /tmp. Ready-made, but cogs a customer installs from community repositories are Python code, so the CPU watch matters here as much as on a runtime. The Audio cog runs Lavalink on Java inside the container, on localhost, so no port; it wants about 1 GB of memory on its own. Not yet tested end to end: covered by the E2E runs. On production as egg #45 (2026-10-31), set from this entry.

bot-discord-tickets.note: Discord Tickets 4.0.52 (GPL-3.0, hosted unmodified), from the project's own Pelican egg, rewritten as PLCN_v3. Runs the project's image pinned to 4.0.52 (upstream offered the moving 4.0, latest and main tags); its start script copies the program into app/ at every start, so app/ is on the file deny list and the image decides what runs. Its one port is the web portal (HTTP_PORT); Wings writes the port and HTTP_EXTERNAL (the server's address) into .env at every start, where upstream wrote the address once at install. Upstream's SUPER (bot owners with power over every server) defaulted to the upstream developer's own Discord ID; now empty. Its install appended a fresh ENCRYPTION_KEY at every reinstall, which makes all encrypted data unreadable; it now writes one only when none is there. Database: sqlite by default, in user/, so it needs nothing; mysql works with a database from the Databases tab (Postgres dropped, Tekkura has no Postgres host). Known gap: the image runs its own start script, so the startup cannot wait for a token the way Muse does; without one it exits, Wings gives up after the second quick exit, and the server reads Offline until the token and secret are in and it is started. Not yet tested end to end: covered by the E2E runs. On production as egg #46 (2026-10-31), set from this entry.
